newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan cuts foreign currency deposit reserve ratio.
newsitem.headline: Jordan cuts foreign currency deposit reserve ratio.

text.p: Jordan's central bank reduced a compulsory reserve requirement on foreign currency deposits with local banks to 14 percent from 35 percent, according to a bank circular obtained by Reuters on Wednesday.

It will however treat the new foreign currency deposits as dinar reserves, which receive no interest payment, the bank's circular said. Prior to the move Jordan Central Bank paid banks interest on the foreign deposit reserves.
The cut, due to be implemented within three months, brings the foreign currency requirements in line with the 14 percent ratio for dinar deposits.

The move in effect will release around $700 million that the central bank was investing and which will now be available for banks to invest in both the domestic market and international capital markets.
A total of 2.367 billion dinars ($3.34 billion) in foreign currency accounts are held by Jordan's 21 licensed banks including six investment banks and five subsidiaries of foreign banks.

Jordan's bank deposits, both local and foreign currency accounts, stood in August at 5.973 billion dinars ($8.45 billion). Year-on-year foreign currency deposits were 10 percent higher than the same month last year, when they stood at 2.153 billion dinars, while total deposits grew only 5.2 percent.
